newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth Q1 buoyed by call services growth.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth Q1 buoyed by call services growth.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Monday a record increase in customer access lines and strong customer growth in its wireless operations at home and abroad produced first quarter earnings that were a penny ahead of expectations.

First quarter revenues from vertical services, or services in addition to basic access, were $295 million, up 29 percent versus a year ago. Sales of new calling features like Caller ID and Call Waiting rose 24 percent.
The company said operating earnings rose 11.1 percent to $0.70 per share versus $0.63 reported a year earlier, excluding a $0.35 gain in the 1996 quarter on the sale of paging operations.
The First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter was $0.69 per share.
Total first quarter revenues rose to $4.85 billion from $4.54 billion a year ago.
"BellSouth's 17th consecutive quarter of improved operating results was driven by our innovative marketing," said Duane Ackerman, president and chief executive officer.
"Sales increased across the board because we're paying close attention to what our customers want," he said.
BellSouth said access lines rose 379,000 in the first quarter, the biggest gain for any quarter in its history. The old mark of 359,000 was set in the 1996 first quarter.
The 4.8 percent annual growth was driven by record demand in the consumer market, it said, with total residential lines growing by a record 254,000 in the first quarter.
Additional residential lines increased 106,000, the first time BellSouth has added more than 100,000 in any quarter.
BellSouth and GTE Corp are consistent leaders among U.S. providers of local and regional phone service in this closely watched measure of growth, analysts said.
The company said its U.S. cellular operations ended the first quarter with 3.8 million customers, an annual growth rate of 24 percent.
In BellSouth's international cellular markets, customers rose 76 percent since the first quarter of 1996, reaching 1.5 million in first quarter 1997.
With the addition of Peru, Nicaragua and Ecuador during the first quarter of 1997, BellSouth now serves cellular markets in 14 countries with 188 million potential customers.
Total operating expenses increased 4.0 percent, primarily reflecting customer growth in wireless.
In BellSouth's telephone operations, cash operating expenses fell 1.6 percent versus the first quarter of 1996.

The company said first quarter revenues from core local service operations rose to $2.1 billion, up nine percent from the $1.9 billion reported in the year-ago quarter. Wireless communications revenues rose 22 percent to $765 million.
Network access lines in service at March 31 rose to 22.5 million from 21.5 million a year earlier.
"These are just blistering numbers," Montgomery analyst Bill Vogel said of BellSouth's growth in customer access lines and the value-added services on top of basic access provision.
"They have not only the access lines growing, but the services on those lines growing sharply," Vogel said.

He said he believes BellSouth earnings will accelerate in coming quarters beyond the 11 percent rise in the latest quarter as core growth and new product introductions offset the limited impact of competition in its local markets.
Vogel maintains a buy rating on the stock, which he labels "cheap" in the vicinity of $41, where it closed Friday. "I am looking for $52 on the stock," he said of his 12-month target.
Bellsouth shares had retreated 1/8 of a point from the opening to 40-7/8 at middday Monday on light volume.
